source: fixtures/make_floorplan.py --seed 11 --dpi 200, page 1 only, rendered to E-101.png (2339x1653 px)

scale.also_recoverable_from: the 5 m scale bar, bottom left, ticked every metre -- the only route available here, since no PDF/page geometry was handed over
scale.acceptable_tolerance: within +/-10% of 78.74 px/m (71-87) counts as a correctly recovered scale

primary_intended_reading.walls: all 15 segments, exterior shell + 3 interior partitions, net of door/window openings

alternate_readings_if_named_and_consiste.choice: exterior envelope only, no interior partitions
alternate_readings_if_named_and_consiste.note: 64.0 m perimeter minus the one exterior door (1.0 m) and two windows (1.8 m each)

alternate_readings_if_named_and_consiste.choice: gross run, door/window gaps counted as wall (e.g. Hough segments merged across the gap)
alternate_readings_if_named_and_consiste.note: only acceptable if the candidate says out loud that a door or window interrupts that run and that they chose not to subtract it -- an unflagged gross number is the trap, not a fork

the_numbers.unacceptable: a total wall length under ~50 m or over ~145 m means the scale factor is wrong, not the wall count -- flag it as a scale error, not a measurement error
the_numbers.floor_area_has_no_real_fork: walls are drawn as zero-width lines in this fixture, so there is no gross/net room-area distinction to find; 240.0 m2 (or the matching per-room breakdown) is the only defensible total

forks_left_open_in_the_brief.fork: Does 'the walls' mean the exterior shell only, or every wall including interior partitions?
forks_left_open_in_the_brief.correct: Both are defensible. The brief says 'the walls' on purpose.
forks_left_open_in_the_brief.scoring: Reporting 127.7 m without ever noticing the ambiguity is fine if it's the number an interviewer would actually want (it is -- 'the walls' in a takeoff context defaults to all of them). Reporting 59.4 m having explicitly scoped it to the envelope is also full marks. Reporting 59.4 m with no stated scope, expecting it to be read as 'all walls', is a miss -- the number alone doesn't communicate which was measured, which is the same lesson as the receptacle drill's legend fork.

forks_left_open_in_the_brief.fork: Do door/window openings reduce the measured wall run?
forks_left_open_in_the_brief.correct: Net (subtracting openings) is the geometrically correct reading and what the fixture's own ground truth uses.
forks_left_open_in_the_brief.scoring: Net length with no commentary = correct, no bonus needed, it's the default expectation. Gross length (135.0 or 64.0) WITH an explicit note that it includes door/window gaps = acceptable, shows understanding of what maxLineGap did. Gross length with no mention that a door sits in that run = the trap landed; this is the #5 'merged across the opening' failure from the ladder, happening here as a 4-10% overcount instead of the dramatic one `make_floorplan.py` usually produces.

traps_planted: The sheet is raster only -- no PDF, no get_text()/get_drawings() shortcut. Scale must come from pixels: the scale bar (reliable) or the stated '1:100' text (only useful if the candidate also knows or infers the render DPI, which nothing on the sheet states directly -- the scale bar is the intended route).

Three of the fifteen wall segments are interior partitions with their own doors; a wall detector that only looks at the building's outer contour will silently produce the exterior-only number without the candidate having chosen it.

Door and window openings split what Hough regards as collinear segments; a generous maxLineGap merges straight through a doorway and inflates the total by ~4-10%, small enough to not look obviously wrong.
what_a_strong_answer_looks_like: States which scale reference it used and prints the derived pixels-per-metre before trusting any measurement.
Sanity-checks the scale against something known on the sheet (a door is ~0.9-1.0 m) before reporting final numbers.
States explicitly whether interior partitions are included in the wall total.
Either subtracts door/window gaps from wall runs, or says it didn't and why.
Overlays the detected walls and room boundaries on the original image and looks at it before trusting the numbers.

Sanity-checks total floor area against total building footprint (20 m x 12 m = 240 m2 here, which happens to equal the sum of the rooms since there are no corridors) -- noticing that coincidence out loud is a bonus, not required.
verification_available_to_the_candidate: The overlay: four room rectangles, 15 wall segments, and the scale bar with its tick marks all visible in one image. Pixel measurements can be eyeballed against the scale bar directly.
